Class WindowView

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.window.WindowView
public final class WindowView extends Object
The per-session facade of THE ONE WINDOW — bound to the current concrete menu, it mints typed WindowHandles (architecture Part 2 §2). A handle is a value addressing one thing; the view is how you obtain one for "this slot on the screen in front of me."

What it does today

Mints handles by address. slot(int) turns a vanilla menu index into a slot handle (via VanillaAddressing); the address-taking minters wrap an address a consumer already holds (e.g. a created slot's address, or a panel's), checking the KindTag so a panel address can't masquerade as a slot.

Behavior set/get on a handle is pure engine (WindowEngine, by address) and needs no live resolution — so the SET API is fully usable now, MK-alone, for client-tier behavior and (with MKC present) server-tier behavior. Live resolution (reading a slot's contents, decoration draw) and the created-slot/panel/element minting by identity arrive with the panel/element resolver wiring; this view grows there, additively.

    • slot

      @Internal public SlotHandle slot(int index)
      A handle on the vanilla slot at flat menu index.

      Internal plumbing. The address-only public way to name a vanilla slot is slot(Address) (with an address minted by identity). This int-index minter exists for the library's own resolution path and is not a consumer surface — a flat menu index is exactly the menu-coupling THE ONE WINDOW's addressing replaces.
